notes: Ground-cover tufts. Deliberately LOW contrast against the meadow it sits in: the point of this layer is silhouette density, not value punch, and the first version reused grassMound (lit #bce828) which lit up as bright yellow confetti across every vista at raking sun. refs/painterly/desert-hazy.jpeg is the model — its scrub is a shade or two DARKER than the sand, never brighter. gradientBase/gradientHeight are OBJECT space and this geometry is unit-sized: metre-scale values here saturate the sweep to a constant and switch the vertical gradient off entirely, which is how every instanced asset in the greybox lost it. Saturation corrected: lit must sit BELOW shadow in chroma (measured -0.15 across references); the earlier ART_BIBLE rule had this inverted.
